abstract: Maintains vehicle configuration, obstacle avoidance instrumentation, and habitat power metrics
system_message:
You are the Traverse vehicle systems lead (ENG). Your business responsibility is to maintain vehicle configuration, obstacle avoidance instrumentation, habitat power metrics, and chassis metallurgy verification across candidate traverse expedition plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains vehicle configuration, obstacle avoidance instrumentation, and habitat power metrics（VEH）
information_points.content:
ENG-VEH-GJQ：For the Segmented dual-track modular hauler, the crevasse detection radar sensor is confirmed installed on the leading traverse tractor unit. The system provides a crevasse detection forward scanning range of 120 m under Antarctic ice-shelf conditions, alongside a continuous primary habitat thermal load requirement of 50 kW for crew living and sleeping modules during baseline subzero transit.
ENG-VEH-NXO：For the Heavy articulated tracked traverse train, the crevasse detection radar sensor is confirmed installed on the leading traverse tractor unit. Under Antarctic ice-shelf conditions, its forward scanning range for surface crevasse detection is 120 m, and its crew living and sleeping modules require a continuous primary habitat thermal load of 40 kW during baseline subzero transit.
ENG-VEH-KOS：For the High-flotation multi-axle wheeled convoy, the crevasse detection radar sensor is confirmed installed on the leading traverse tractor unit. Sensor calibration tests indicate a crevasse detection forward scanning range of 80 m under Antarctic ice-shelf conditions, with a continuous primary habitat thermal load of 40 kW needed for crew living and sleeping modules during baseline subzero transit.

information_points.title: Chassis metallurgy verification（CHASSIS）
information_points.content:
ENG-CHASSIS-6YG：Metallurgical stress testing of the primary load-bearing structural frame for the Segmented dual-track modular hauler confirms a steel ductile-to-brittle transition temperature of -40 degC.
ENG-CHASSIS-M0J：Metallurgical stress testing of the primary load-bearing structural frame for the Heavy articulated tracked traverse train confirms a steel ductile-to-brittle transition temperature of -50 degC.
ENG-CHASSIS-4PH：Metallurgical stress testing of the primary load-bearing structural frame for the High-flotation multi-axle wheeled convoy confirms a steel ductile-to-brittle transition temperature of -60 degC.
